study_design: Randomized supplementation trial with prospective postintervention registry follow-up
cohort_total_n_excerpt: To determine the postintervention effects of α-tocopherol and β-carotene, 25,563 men were followed 18 years for cancer incidence and all causes of mortality through national registers.
reason: The abstract analyzes total incident prostate cancer. It does not report an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal incident prostate cancer endpoint. Prostate cancer mortality is a mortality endpoint and is not evidence of aggressive incidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: There were 2,321 incident prostate cancers during the 18-year post-trial follow-up among the 25,389 participants who had no prostate cancer diagnosed by the end of the intervention. No difference in incidence was observed between α-tocopherol recipients and nonrecipients (RR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.89–1.05) or between β-carotene recipients and nonrecipients (RR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.95–1.12) (Table 2).
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied full-text evidence identifies the β-carotene estimate as total incident prostate cancer; the abstract does not report the β-carotene prostate cancer effect.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: For prostate cancer (n = 2,321), RR was 0.97 (95% CI, 0.89-1.05) among α-tocopherol recipients compared with nonrecipients with the preventive effect of α-tocopherol continuing ∼8 years postintervention.
estimate_classifications.reason: This is an estimate for total prostate cancer incidence, without an aggressive disease restriction.
